text:
alex: FYI the auto-scale run for gpufleet in us-east-2 hit a hard stop during terraform plan. subnet in az-b reports 0 allocatable IPs. putting any module upgrades on hold until we confirm a migration path :warning:

maya: ugh. which subnet exactly? is this the new secondary pool change from last week? :eyes:

alex: it's the gpupool-secondary-us-east-2b (module: gpufleet/v2). plan error attached below from the CI run. ci-bot posted the build too.

jin: can you paste the plan snippet? I want to see the specific error (allocation vs. attachment)

alex: ```
Error: creating Subnet: InsufficientFreeAddressesInSubnet: The subnet does not have enough free addresses
  status code: 400, request id: 9f3b5e3c

  on modules/gpufleet/subnet.tf line 42, in resource "aws_subnet" "secondary":
  42: resource "aws_subnet" "secondary" {
```

sam: This looks like the module's default `secondary_cidr_mask` was changed from `/20` -> `/24` in the last version bump. We didn't catch it because the plan was only run for new stacks. That would explain the exhaustion.

maya: ohhh. so nodes are trying to scale into the smaller subnet and there's no headroom. we should not revert module if we can migrate IPs; reverting would rollback other fixes.

jin: migration plan idea: 1) provision new secondary subnets with /20 size in the same AZ (as ephemeral resources), 2) update gpupool module to reference the new subnet ids, 3) do `terraform state mv`/`import` for any existing instances that need to be re-associated, 4) scale down old pools and deprovision old subnets.

sam: agree. rough commands: ```bash
# create new subnet via tf var override or a small module
TF_VAR_new_secondary_cidr="10.10.0.0/20" terraform apply -target=module.gpufleet.secondary_subnet
# import existing ENIs / route tables if needed
terraform import module.gpufleet.aws_subnet.secondary subnet-0a1b2c3d
# update module refs
terraform plan -var 'use_new_secondary=true'
```

alex: CI note — the gitops pipeline is currently set to auto-approve infra PRs matching `gpufleet/*`. ci-bot, please disable auto-merge for gpufleet changes until we mark the migration complete.

ci-bot: infra-automerge disabled for path `modules/gpufleet/**` by request of alex.

ops-oncall: scheduling a short maintenance window tonight at 23:00 UTC to run the `apply` with the new subnets and perform validation (canary pool first). I'll post the runbook in #incidents.

maya: also add a reconciler guard in our gitops bot to fail fast if `secondary_cidr_mask` shrinks compared to the previous lockfile. Would have prevented this drift.

jin: I'll open a small PR to add that check to the plan-guard CI job and a tfsec-like rule. tagging @sam for review.

sam: will review. also suggest we add a cost note: moving to /20 will increase IP address usage but it's minimal compared to outage risk. add to PR.

alex: thanks all. sequence: disable automerge (done), provision new subnets (jin/sam), run canary apply (ops-oncall), validate scaling, then full rollout. keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
